node.title: Re: Parse a text file with oneliner
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
Have a look at [doc://perlrun] and the -F switch, it's similar to awk, except it splits into the array @F:

perl -F: -lane 'print $F[0] if /^[A-Z]/' infile

Now you could pipe that through [man://sort], or with some trickery you can have Perl do that for you too (see the "Eskimo greeting" in [mod://perlsecret]):

perl -F: -lane 'push @x, $F[0] if /^[A-Z]/}{print for sort @x' infile

This should produce the same output as your first grep | awk | sort command.
